properties.natural_language: Before classification via EDGE-AUTHOR-SUBMIT, the EIP Author must provide a valid EIP with content sufficient to determine its target protocol layer
After classification, every EIP must be assigned to exactly one primary layer: Consensus, Networking, API/RPC, or Applications
The classification action must produce exactly one output state; an EIP cannot simultaneously belong to multiple primary layers
Before evaluating partition risk via EDGE-PROPOSE-CONSENSUS-CHANGE, core developers must submit a properly classified consensus layer EIP
After partition risk evaluation, the network state must resolve to either unified or partitioned; no intermediate state is permitted
A consensus change must always undergo partition risk evaluation before being accepted; no bypass path exists from proposed to unified state
Before the eth/64 handshake via EDGE-SEND-STATUS, a TCP connection must be established and both peers must support eth/64 capability
After ForkID validation, the handshake must terminate in either HANDSHAKE-COMPLETE or PEER-DISCONNECTED; no connection may remain in an ambiguous state
The handshake state machine must enforce strict sequencing: TCP-CONNECTED -> SEND-STATUS -> RECEIVE-STATUS -> STATUS-EXCHANGED -> VALIDATE-FORKID; no steps may be skipped
Before ForkID comparison via EDGE-COMPUTE, the remote ForkID [forkHash, forkNext] must be successfully parsed from the peer Status message
After ForkHash comparison, exactly one of FORKHASH-MATCH or FORKHASH-MISMATCH must result; for matches, ForkNext must also be checked
Before protocol version negotiation, both peers must have completed the devp2p RLPx Hello exchange with capability lists
After negotiation, exactly one of eth/64, eth/63 fallback, or no common version must be selected; eth/64 is preferred when mutually supported
Before transitioning from Frontier to Homestead, the block height must be verified against the hardcoded activation block (1,150,000 mainnet)
After the Homestead activation block is reached, all subsequent blocks must be validated under Homestead rules including EIP-2, EIP-7, and EIP-8
The fork transition is irreversible: once STATE-POST-HOMESTEAD is reached, the system must never return to STATE-PRE-HOMESTEAD
Before block validation via EDGE-PEER-SENDS-BLOCK, the block must be received from a network peer with valid header structure
After fork rule determination, the correct validation path (Frontier or Homestead) must be chosen exclusively based on block number comparison to 1,150,000
Every validated block must reach exactly one of BLOCK-VALID or BLOCK-INVALID; no block may remain in an indeterminate validation state
Before executing DUPN/SWAPN/EXCHANGE, the gas cost of 3 must be available; insufficient gas must halt execution immediately
After successful stack manipulation, the program counter must advance by exactly 2 (opcode + immediate byte) before fetching the next instruction
The execution pipeline must enforce sequential validation: gas check -> immediate read -> decode -> range validation -> stack depth check -> execute; no step may be reordered or skipped
DUPN must duplicate stack[n] to top, SWAPN must swap stack[0] with stack[n+1], and EXCHANGE must swap stack[n+1] with stack[m+1]; each opcode's semantics are mutually exclusive
Before decoding the operand, the byte must be checked against disallowed ranges to avoid conflicts with JUMPDEST (0x5b) and PUSH (0x60-0x7f) opcodes
After range validation passes, decode_single must map operand to stack index in range [17, 235] for DUPN/SWAPN, and decode_pair must produce valid (n, m) pair for EXCHANGE
Operands in the JUMPDEST/PUSH conflict range must always produce STATE-RANGE-CONFLICT-5B or STATE-RANGE-CONFLICT-PUSH; they must never reach RANGE-VALID
After stack depth validation, operations must only proceed if the required depth is met: n <= len(stack) for DUPN, n+1 <= len(stack) for SWAPN, m+1 <= len(stack) for EXCHANGE
Before exceptional halt processing, the specific halt cause (invalid range or stack underflow) must be identified and recorded
After any exceptional halt, all remaining gas in the current frame must be consumed and the call frame must be reverted before notifying the caller
Both exceptional halt paths (range error and stack underflow) must converge to the same gas consumption and frame revert sequence; no halt may bypass gas consumption

Before processing a signing request via EDGE-RECEIVE-REQUEST, the dApp must provide a valid typed data JSON structure with types, primaryType, domain, and message fields along with a 20-byte account address
Before signing, the account must be unlocked; locked accounts must return an error and never proceed to hash computation or signing
After user approval and hash computation, the signing operation must produce a valid 65-byte ECDSA signature (r, s, v) over the typed data hash
User consent is mandatory: the signing pipeline must always pass through AWAITING-APPROVAL before any hash computation or private key usage occurs
Before encoding, the raw typed data must contain valid type definitions with no circular references and all referenced types must be defined
After encoding completes, the final hash must be exactly keccak256(0x19 || 0x01 || domainSeparator || hashStruct(message)), producing a 32-byte output
The encoding pipeline must produce deterministic output: identical typed data inputs must always yield the same final hash regardless of JSON key ordering
Domain separator encoding must execute independently from message struct encoding; both paths from RAW-TYPED-DATA must converge at COMPUTE-FINAL-HASH
Before a replay attack can succeed, the attacker must capture a valid signature and the target application must lack application-level nonce protection
After domain separator verification, cross-domain replay attempts must always fail with DOMAIN-MISMATCH; only same-domain replays may proceed to nonce checking
The domain separator must always prevent cross-contract and cross-chain signature reuse; DOMAIN-MISMATCH is the only valid outcome for different-domain replay attempts
After application nonce check, same-domain replay must be blocked if nonce tracking is implemented; applications without replay protection remain vulnerable
Before executing upgrade_to_electra, the current epoch must equal ELECTRA_FORK_EPOCH and the beacon state must be in valid Deneb format

After the upgrade completes, all Electra-specific fields must be initialized: earliest_exit_epoch computed, exit_balance_to_consume set, pending_deposits populated from inactive validators and excess balances
The upgrade sequence must execute atomically and in strict order: upgrade -> compute exit epoch -> compute churn -> queue deposits -> queue excess -> complete; partial upgrades are not permitted
Before fork version validation, the previous fork metadata must be readable and contain valid Deneb version information
After fork version update, previous_version must equal old current_version, current_version must equal ELECTRA_FORK_VERSION, and epoch must equal ELECTRA_FORK_EPOCH
Before deposit queue migration, inactive validators must have activation_epoch == FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH and effective_balance > 0
After migration, each inactive validator must have effective_balance set to 0 and a corresponding PendingDeposit entry with correct pubkey, credentials, amount, and slot
Total balance must be conserved during migration: the sum of all validator balances plus pending deposit amounts must remain constant before and after the operation
Before account creation nonce increment, a CREATE or contract creation transaction must be initiated with valid parameters
After nonce increment, the new account must have nonce=1 before init code execution begins, preventing the account from being classified as empty during creation
Before empty account cleanup, all touched accounts during the transaction must be tracked and the transaction execution must be complete
After cleanup, every touched account that has no code, zero nonce, and zero balance must be deleted from state; non-empty accounts must be preserved
An account is empty if and only if it has no code AND nonce == 0 AND balance == 0; this three-part condition must be evaluated atomically
Before the conditional gas charge is evaluated, a CALL/CALLCODE/DELEGATECALL must be initiated to a destination address
After evaluation, the 25,000 gas charge must be applied if and only if the destination is dead AND value > 0; all other cases must not incur extra gas
Before revert handling, the transaction must have pending account deletions from the current execution context
After transaction revert, all account deletions from the reverted transaction must be undone and accounts restored to their pre-transaction state
Before block construction, the validator must be the selected proposer for the current slot and must gather expected withdrawals from beacon state
After block assembly, the execution payload must include all expected withdrawals and the block must be signed and broadcast to the P2P network
The execution engine must faithfully include all specified withdrawals in the produced payload; any deviation constitutes a consensus violation
Before submitting a BLS credential change, the validator must currently have BLS_WITHDRAWAL_PREFIX (0x00) credentials and possess the BLS withdrawal secret key
After signing, the SignedBLSToExecutionChange must contain validator_index, from_bls_pubkey, to_execution_address, and a valid BLS signature from the withdrawal key
BLS credential changes are irreversible: once the credential prefix changes from 0x00 to execution address prefix, subsequent change attempts for the same validator must be rejected
Before partial withdrawal, the validator must be active with balance exceeding MAX_EFFECTIVE_BALANCE and have eth1 (execution) withdrawal credentials
After withdrawal computation, partial withdrawals must equal balance minus MAX_EFFECTIVE_BALANCE, and full withdrawals must equal the entire remaining balance
Before light client store upgrade, the store must contain valid Deneb-format data including finalized header and sync committee information
After upgrade, the light client store must contain Electra-format headers with normalized merkle branches and preserved core fields (sync committees, max active participants)
Before merkle branch normalization, the Deneb-format branch must be valid and the Electra generalized index must be known to compute required depth
After normalization, the branch must be padded with zero-bytes (Bytes32()) to match the depth required by Electra's generalized index (floorlog2)
Before processing pre-fork light client data from the network via EDGE-NETWORK-RECEIVE, the data must be received from P2P peers and identified as Deneb-format
After local upgrade of network-received pre-fork data, the resulting Electra-format data must be functionally equivalent to data that would have been produced natively in Electra format

Pre-fork data from external network sources must always pass through local upgrade functions before being used by Electra light client logic; direct use of Deneb-format data in Electra context is prohibited
Before ENR signing, the record content must be assembled with a valid sequence number and key-value pairs in sorted order
After signing, the ENR must contain a valid 64-byte secp256k1 signature (r || s, no recovery ID) over the keccak256 hash of the content
The ENR encoding pipeline must preserve data integrity: unsigned -> hash -> sign -> RLP encode -> base64 encode; the text format must always start with 'enr:' prefix
Before ENR validation, raw ENR data must be received from an external source (peer, DNS, or ENS) and enter the validation pipeline
After all validation checks pass (size <= 300 bytes, valid RLP, sorted unique keys, known identity scheme, valid signature), the ENR must be accepted
Any validation failure (size exceeded, malformed RLP, invalid signature) must immediately reject the record; no partial validation results may be accepted
The ENR size limit of 300 bytes must be enforced as the first validation check before any decoding or cryptographic operations to prevent resource exhaustion
Before processing untrusted ENR data from external sources (DNS, P2P, ENS) via boundary edges, cryptographic validation must be performed to establish identity binding
After cryptographic binding validation, the node identity must be verified and the 64-byte node address derived from keccak256 of the public key
ENR data must cross the trust boundary only through cryptographic signature validation; connectivity information must never be extracted from unsigned or invalidly signed records
DNS spoofing can redirect to malicious ENRs but cannot forge valid signatures; the crypto validation limits the impact of transport-layer attacks to denial of service
